title: rorca-mcp-cli
_notes: Adds the missing end-to-end workflow tools: rorca_forge_and_run (single MCP tool that goes brief → spec → approve → run → completion), rorca_cancel_run, and CLI commands (rorca forge, rorca run, rorca status). The individual tools (rorca_generate_spec, rorca_approve_spec, rorca_trigger_run, rorca_run_status) already exist in backend/src/mcp/server.ts. This spec layers the combined workflow on top and adds the terminal CLI entry points. EXPANDED 2026-03-11: 8 stories, 180+ total ACs covering all error categories, TTY/non-TTY modes, VS Code extension activation events, resolveTreeItem, offline handling, shell completion, and CI/CD integration.
_executionOrder: After rorca-convention-agents TK-001. Can run in parallel with rorca-integrations since it touches different files (mcp/server.ts + CLI entry point, not integration routes). MC-001 first (foundation), MC-002 depends on MC-001, MC-003 depends on MC-001+MC-002, MC-004 independent, MC-005 depends on MC-003, MC-006 depends on MC-004, MC-007 depends on MC-004, MC-008 depends on MC-003.

userStories.title: rorca_forge_and_run — Brief-to-Completion Single MCP Tool
userStories.description: Add rorca_forge_and_run to backend/src/mcp/server.ts. This is the one-shot tool: accepts a plain-English brief and workspace_id, internally sequences rorca_generate_spec → rorca_approve_spec → rorca_trigger_run → subscribes to SSE /api/pipeline/stream until run_finished event (with 15s polling fallback), and returns a structured completion result. MCP progress notifications are emitted at each phase so the calling model sees live updates. This is the primary tool for the 'I have an idea, build it' workflow from inside a Claude Code or OpenCode session.
acceptanceCriteria: rorca_forge_and_run registered in mcp/server.ts with inputSchema: { brief: z.string().min(10).describe('Plain-English description of what to build'), workspace_id: z.string().describe('Workspace ID from rorca_list_workspaces'), model: z.string().optional().describe('Execution model override'), spec_model: z.string().optional().describe('Spec generation model override'), auto_worktree: z.boolean().optional().default(true).describe('Run in isolated git worktree'), timeout_minutes: z.number().optional().default(90).describe('Max runtime in minutes (1-480)') }

Tool internally sequences: POST /api/specs/generate → POST /api/specs/:id/approve → POST /api/pipeline/trigger, then subscribes to SSE /api/pipeline/stream filtered by spec_id for live story events; falls back to polling GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id status every 15s if SSE connection fails with ECONNREFUSED or times out on connection attempt

MCP progress notifications emitted via server.notification({ method: 'notifications/progress', params: { progressToken, progress, total, message } }) at each phase: spec_generating (progress:0, message: 'Generating spec from brief...') → spec_generated (progress:1, message: 'Spec generated: N stories') → pipeline_started (progress:2, message: 'Pipeline started, run #ID') → per-story events (incrementing progress, message: '✓ US-001 Title (Ns)' or '✗ US-001 Title (failed)') → complete (progress:total, message: 'Complete: N passed, M failed')

Returns on full success: { ok: true, spec_id: string, spec_title: string, story_count: number, run_id: number, passed: number, failed: number, skipped: number, branch: string | null, worktree_path: string | null, elapsed_seconds: number, stories: Array<{ id: string, title: string, status: 'passed'|'failed'|'skipped', elapsed_seconds: number, retries: number }> }

On spec generation failure, returns isError:true result with category-specific message using the 8 error categories from specs.ts: { ok: false, phase: 'spec_generation', error: string, category: 'model_error'|'api_key_error'|'rate_limit'|'context_too_large'|'timeout'|'parse_error'|'network_error'|'unknown', suggestion: string } — does NOT throw a protocol-level error, returns content with isError:true so the calling LLM can read the error and decide next steps
On api_key_error from spec generation: suggestion field reads 'Check your API key in Rorca Settings > API Keys or run rorca_update_direction to verify your configuration'
On rate_limit from spec generation: suggestion field reads 'Rate limit reached. Try again in 60 seconds or switch to a different model using the spec_model parameter'
On context_too_large from spec generation: suggestion field reads 'Brief or direction stack too long. Shorten the brief or reduce L1/L2 direction layers via rorca_update_direction'

On parse_error from spec generation: tool automatically retries spec generation once with same parameters before returning error; if second attempt also fails, returns error with suggestion 'The model returned invalid JSON. Try spec_model: claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 which has reliable JSON output'

On pipeline trigger conflict (existing run active for workspace): returns { ok: false, phase: 'pipeline_trigger', error: 'A run is already active for this workspace', active_run_id: number, suggestion: 'Use rorca_cancel_run to stop the active run first, or wait for it to complete' }

On ECONNREFUSED (Rorca server not reachable at any phase): returns { ok: false, phase: string, error: 'Cannot connect to Rorca server at http://localhost:3030', suggestion: 'Run: rorca start — to launch the Rorca server' }

Timeout behavior: if timeout_minutes is exceeded, calls POST /api/pipeline/runs/:id/cancel internally, then returns { ok: false, phase: 'timeout', error: 'Run exceeded timeout_minutes limit', partial_results: { passed, failed, skipped, stories } }
The tool respects the progressToken from the MCP request params; if no progressToken is provided, progress notifications are sent with progressToken: null (no-op on client side but harmless)

SSE subscription: connects to /api/pipeline/stream?spec_id=<id>&run_id=<id>, listens for story_passed, story_failed, story_skipped, run_finished event types; on run_finished event stops polling immediately without waiting for next 15s interval

SSE reconnect: if SSE connection drops mid-run (EventSource error or network blip), falls back to polling every 15s using GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId for status, then switches back to SSE if reconnection succeeds within 30s

Tool is available in both stdio MCP server (mcp/server.ts) and HTTP transport at /mcp (auto-generated from OpenAPI @swagger annotation on a new POST /api/mcp/forge-and-run route with same response contract)

If workspace_id does not exist in the database, returns { ok: false, phase: 'validation', error: 'Workspace not found: <workspace_id>', suggestion: 'Use rorca_list_workspaces to see available workspace IDs' }
If brief is fewer than 10 characters, returns { ok: false, phase: 'validation', error: 'Brief is too short (minimum 10 characters)', suggestion: 'Provide a detailed description of what to build' }
If timeout_minutes is outside 1-480 range, returns { ok: false, phase: 'validation', error: 'timeout_minutes must be between 1 and 480' }

If model string is provided but not in the SUPPORTED_MODELS list from llm-client.ts, returns { ok: false, phase: 'validation', error: 'Unsupported model: <model>', suggestion: 'Use rorca_list_specs or GET /api/direction/models to see supported models' }
On model_error from spec generation (model does not exist or is misconfigured): suggestion reads 'Check the model name in Rorca Settings or use the default by omitting the spec_model parameter'

On network_error from spec generation (connection/endpoint issues during LLM call): returns { ok: false, phase: 'spec_generation', error: 'LLM API network error', category: 'network_error', suggestion: 'Check your internet connection and API provider status. The brief has NOT been processed.' }

On unknown error category from spec generation: returns { ok: false, phase: 'spec_generation', error: 'Unexpected error during spec generation', category: 'unknown', raw_error: first-200-chars-of-error-message }

After rorca_trigger_run is called (pipeline started), if the rorca backend itself crashes and becomes unreachable mid-run, the tool returns { ok: false, phase: 'monitoring', error: 'Lost connection to Rorca server mid-run', run_id: number, suggestion: 'Run: rorca status <run-id> after restarting the server to check run state. The pipeline process may still be running.' }

The tool description in the MCP tool registration reads: 'One-shot: brief → spec → approve → run → completion. Handles the full pipeline end-to-end. Returns structured results when done. Use for: I have an idea, build it. NOT for: monitoring existing runs (use rorca_run_status) or retrying failed stories (use rorca_retry_story).'

The auto_worktree parameter description clarifies the tradeoff: 'Run in isolated git worktree (default: true). When true, pipeline runs in a new branch feat/<spec-slug>-<timestamp> — safe for parallel execution. When false, runs in the current working directory of the workspace — faster but blocks same-workspace parallel runs.'

Tool execution is non-blocking at the MCP protocol level: the tool DOES block the tool call connection for the duration (up to timeout_minutes) but returns a final structured result — the LLM calling it should be aware this is a long-running operation and not chain other tool calls immediately after until this one resolves

If auto_worktree is true and git worktree creation fails (e.g. detached HEAD state, no commits yet in repo), falls back to running in workspace root without worktree and includes { worktree_fallback: true, worktree_error: 'reason' } in the result to inform the caller

If spec generation succeeds but approve fails (e.g. file permission error writing to approved/), returns { ok: false, phase: 'approve', spec_id: string, error: 'Failed to approve spec', detail: error-message } — spec is NOT deleted so user can manually approve via rorca_approve_spec

elapsed_seconds in the success response is wall clock time from tool invocation start to completion, not sum of story times — includes spec generation time (~30-60s), pipeline trigger latency, and all story execution times
The tool registers with the MCP server using category annotation in the description so it appears in the 'Specs & Pipeline' group in the /api/mcp/tools endpoint and VS Code tree view (MC-004)

userStories.title: rorca_cancel_run MCP Tool
userStories.description: Add rorca_cancel_run to mcp/server.ts. Accepts { run_id } and calls POST /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/cancel which sends SIGTERM to the pipeline process PID (stored in pipeline_runs), waits up to 5s, then escalates to SIGKILL, marks the run as cancelled in pipeline_runs, and returns a structured result. The existing cancel endpoint already implements the SIGTERM→SIGKILL pattern with 5s grace period and broadcasts run_cancelled WAL event. This tool completes the control surface alongside rorca_trigger_run.
acceptanceCriteria: rorca_cancel_run registered in mcp/server.ts with inputSchema: { run_id: z.number().int().positive().describe('Pipeline run ID to cancel — use rorca_list_runs to find active run IDs') }
Calls POST /api/pipeline/runs/:id/cancel — the existing endpoint that sends SIGTERM to the process group (-pid) and escalates to SIGKILL after 5s if process is still alive

On success returns: { ok: true, run_id: number, status: 'cancelled', message: 'Run #N cancelled', stories_completed: number, stories_remaining: number } — the stories counts are derived from story_results rows for this run_id (passed + skipped = completed, not_started = remaining)
If run_id is not found in pipeline_runs, returns isError:true content: { ok: false, error: 'Run #N not found', suggestion: 'Use rorca_list_runs to see recent run IDs' }

If run is already in terminal state (status = 'completed'|'failed'|'cancelled'), returns: { ok: false, already_terminal: true, status: existing_status, message: 'Run #N is already status — no action taken' } — not an error, just informational (isError: false)

If the process PID recorded in pipeline_runs is not alive (race condition where process died between status check and cancel call), the endpoint still succeeds: marks run as cancelled in DB and returns ok:true with message 'Process had already exited; marked as cancelled in database'
If the cancel API call itself returns non-2xx (e.g. 500 from unexpected DB error), returns isError:true: { ok: false, error: 'Cancel request failed: <status> <body>' }
On ECONNREFUSED (Rorca server unreachable), returns isError:true: { ok: false, error: 'Cannot connect to Rorca server', suggestion: 'Run: rorca start' }
Available in both stdio MCP server and HTTP /mcp transport

rorca_cancel_run tool description reads: 'Cancel an active pipeline run. Sends SIGTERM to the process, waits 5s, then SIGKILL. Marks run as cancelled in database. Safe to call even if process already exited — idempotent cancel.'

Response always includes stories_completed and stories_remaining counts; these are computed as: stories_completed = COUNT(*) FROM story_results WHERE run_id=N AND status IN ('pass','skip'), stories_remaining = total_story_count_from_spec_json - stories_completed

When cancelling an already-cancelled run (idempotent call), tool returns { ok: true, already_cancelled: true, message: 'Run #N was already cancelled', stories_completed, stories_remaining } with isError: false — callers can safely call cancel multiple times

After cancel call succeeds, tool waits up to 2s and verifies via GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id that status is now 'cancelled' in DB before returning — prevents race where response arrives before DB update completes

rorca_cancel_run inputSchema description includes example usage note: 'To find active run IDs: use rorca_list_runs and look for status: running. To cancel the run started by rorca_forge_and_run, use the run_id from its response.'

userStories.title: rorca CLI — forge, run, and status Commands
userStories.description: Extend the rorca CLI in bin/rorca.ts with forge, run, and status subcommands. These make the full Rorca loop usable from any terminal without opening the UI — designed to pair directly with Claude Code and OpenCode CLI sessions. Supports both TTY mode (progress spinners on stderr, colored output) and non-TTY/CI mode (plain text on stdout, structured JSON with --json flag). API URL is resolved via --api-url flag → RORCA_API_URL env var → ~/.rorca/config.json apiUrl field → http://localhost:3030 default.
acceptanceCriteria:
rorca forge '<brief>' --workspace <path> generates spec via POST /api/specs/generate and prints to stdout: '
Spec generated: rorca-my-feature

  US-001  Add payment model
  US-002  Stripe webhook handler
  ...

N stories total. Run with: rorca forge '<brief>' --workspace <path> --run' — workspace path is resolved to workspace ID via GET /api/workspaces then matched by path

rorca forge ... --run triggers pipeline after generation via POST /api/pipeline/trigger and streams story events: in TTY mode prints colored lines to stderr ('  ⠋ US-001 Add payment model...'), updating in place with ora spinner; on story completion replaces spinner line with '  ✓ US-001 Add payment model (2m 14s)' (green) or '  ✗ US-003 Stripe webhook (failed, 3 retries)' (red)

In non-TTY mode (process.stdout.isTTY === false or NO_COLOR env var set), rorca forge --run prints one line per story event to stdout without ANSI codes: 'story_started US-001 Add payment model' then 'story_passed US-001 Add payment model 134s' — suitable for grep/awk in scripts

rorca forge --json <brief> --workspace <path> [--run] outputs ONLY valid JSON to stdout at completion: { specId: string, specTitle: string, storyCount: number, runId: number|null, passed: number|null, failed: number|null, elapsed: number|null, stories: Array<{id, title, status, elapsed}> } — progress updates go to stderr as plain text even in JSON mode

rorca run <spec-id> --workspace <path> triggers an existing approved spec via POST /api/pipeline/trigger and streams the same TTY/non-TTY story progress as rorca forge --run; if spec is in 'pending' state (not approved), prints error: 'Spec rorca-my-feature is pending approval. Approve it first with: rorca approve rorca-my-feature' and exits 1

rorca status <run-id> prints a formatted table: run ID, spec title, status, elapsed time, passed/total stories — uses GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id; if run-id not found, prints 'Run #N not found. Use: rorca status to see all recent runs' and exits 1; if run-id is omitted, lists last 10 runs from GET /api/pipeline/runs

API URL resolution chain (in priority order): (1) --api-url <url> CLI flag, (2) RORCA_API_URL environment variable, (3) apiUrl field in ~/.rorca/config.json, (4) fallback to http://localhost:3030 — all four tiers checked at CLI startup; selected URL printed to stderr in --verbose mode

On ECONNREFUSED at any command, prints to stderr: '
✗ Cannot connect to Rorca at <url>
  Start the server: rorca start
  Or set a different URL: rorca --api-url http://your-server:3030 <command>
' and exits with code 2 (system error, not user error)

Exit codes: 0 (all stories passed or command succeeded), 1 (user error: bad args, spec not found, any story failed), 2 (system error: ECONNREFUSED, unexpected 5xx, process signal), 130 (SIGINT — user pressed Ctrl+C, cleanup then exit 130 per Unix convention)

SIGINT handling: when user presses Ctrl+C during rorca forge --run or rorca run, prints '

Interrupted. Run is still active in Rorca. To cancel: rorca cancel <run-id>
' and exits 130 — does NOT automatically cancel the run (user may want it to continue)

rorca forge --help prints usage with example: '
  Examples:
    # Generate a spec from a brief
    rorca forge "Add Stripe payment integration" --workspace ./my-app

    # Generate and immediately run
    rorca forge "Add Stripe payment integration" --workspace ./my-app --run

    # JSON output for CI
    rorca forge --json "Add auth" --workspace ./my-app --run | jq .passed
'

NO_COLOR env var respected across all commands: if set (any value), disables all ANSI escape codes in all output including spinner, colored story pass/fail indicators, and table borders — output is plain ASCII

rorca status with --watch flag polls GET /api/pipeline/runs/:id every 5s and re-renders the status table in-place (terminal clear + reprint) until run reaches terminal state (completed/failed/cancelled); exits 0 if completed, exits 1 if failed

All long-running operations (forge --run, run, status --watch) print elapsed time updated every second to the right side of the current spinner line in TTY mode: '  ⠋ US-001 Add payment model... (47s)'

rorca approve <spec-id> --workspace <path> calls POST /api/specs/:id/approve and prints '✓ Spec rorca-my-feature approved — ready to run' — this subcommand is needed as companion to forge without --run

rorca forge without --workspace prints: '
✗ --workspace is required

  Usage: rorca forge '<brief>' --workspace <path>
  Example: rorca forge "Add auth" --workspace ./my-app
' to stderr and exits 1 — error message always goes to stderr, not stdout

rorca forge --workspace with a path that has no registered Rorca workspace prints: '✗ No Rorca workspace found at /path/to/dir\n  Register it first: open http://localhost:3030 and add the workspace' and exits 1
When spec generation takes more than 10s in TTY mode, the CLI updates the spinner text to 'Generating spec... (Ns elapsed)' every second so user knows it is not frozen

rorca forge --model <model> flag overrides the execution model for the pipeline trigger; rorca forge --spec-model <model> flag overrides the spec generation model — both optional, default is workspace L3 preferred_model then llm-client DEFAULT_MODEL

rorca run <spec-id> where spec-id is in 'done' (all stories passed) state prints: 'Spec rorca-my-feature already completed (all stories passed). Use rorca forge to create a new spec or rorca run --force to re-run.' and exits 0 — not an error

rorca run <spec-id> --force re-runs even if spec is done by resetting passes:false on all stories before triggering; prints warning '⚠ Re-running completed spec — story pass states reset' in amber in TTY mode
All rorca commands print their version and API URL in --verbose mode before any action: '[rorca v1.0.0 → http://localhost:3030]' to stderr

userStories.title: MCP Tools Tree View in rorca VS Code Extension
userStories.description: Add a 'MCP Tools' tree view panel to the rorca VS Code extension. The tree view lists all available rorca MCP tools grouped by category (Specs & Pipeline, Story Editing, Direction Stack, Workspaces, Memory), with each tool showing its name and a one-line description. The tool list is fetched from GET /api/mcp/tools on the rorca backend. Items have inline action buttons (copy name, insert call syntax, run tool). Implements resolveTreeItem for async tooltip loading. Handles offline/degraded mode with cached tool list and 'Start Rorca server' action.
acceptanceCriteria: A new GET /api/mcp/tools endpoint exists on the backend returning: { tools: Array<{ name: string, description: string, category: string, inputSchema: Record<string, unknown>, requiredParams: string[] }> } with all 24 MCP tools grouped into exactly 5 categories: 'Specs & Pipeline' (9 tools), 'Story Editing' (4 tools), 'Direction Stack' (3 tools), 'Workspaces' (4 tools), 'Memory' (3 tools) plus the new MC-001/MC-002 tools appended to 'Specs & Pipeline'

The rorca VS Code extension registers a TreeDataProvider class RorcaMcpToolsProvider implementing vscode.TreeDataProvider<MrcpTreeItem> with getTreeItem(element) and getChildren(element?) methods; provider registered via vscode.window.registerTreeDataProvider('rorcaMcpTools', provider) in the extension's activate() function

package.json contributes a view container: { 'rorca': { title: 'Rorca', icon: 'resources/rorca.svg' } } with view: { 'id': 'rorcaMcpTools', 'name': 'MCP Tools', 'contextualTitle': 'Rorca MCP Tools', 'when': 'true' } under 'explorer' viewsContainer
package.json activation events include 'onView:rorcaMcpTools' so extension activates when user opens the tree view panel, even if no editor is open

Tree renders two-level hierarchy: Category nodes (collapsible, TreeItemCollapsibleState.Collapsed by default for 'Memory' and 'Direction Stack', Expanded for 'Specs & Pipeline') → Tool nodes (leaf, TreeItemCollapsibleState.None) with label = tool name and description = short description (first 60 chars)

Inline action buttons on each tool node via contextValue: tool nodes have contextValue = 'rorcaMcpTool'; package.json menus contribution adds buttons to 'view/item/context' with when clause 'viewItem == rorcaMcpTool && view == rorcaMcpTools': (1) Copy Name icon button (files icon, title 'Copy Tool Name'), (2) Insert Call icon button (insert icon, title 'Insert at Cursor') — both appear as inline icons to the right of the tree item label

resolveTreeItem(item, element) implemented on the provider: returns updated TreeItem with tooltip set to a MarkdownString containing the tool's full description, required parameters list, and example call syntax — tooltip is not populated in getTreeItem() (lazy loading) to avoid blocking the initial tree render

Copy Name action: copies tool name string to vscode.env.clipboard and shows vscode.window.showInformationMessage('Copied rorca_tool_name to clipboard') — information message appears in VS Code notification area (not status bar)

Insert Call action: if vscode.window.activeTextEditor exists, inserts tool name at current cursor position using editor.edit(editBuilder => editBuilder.insert(editor.selection.active, toolName)); if no active editor, shows vscode.window.showWarningMessage('Open a file to insert the tool name')

The tree view refreshes (this._onDidChangeTreeData.fire(undefined)) when: (a) extension detects Rorca server comes back online after being offline, (b) user triggers 'Rorca: Refresh MCP Tools' command (registered as rorca.refreshMcpTools), (c) automatic refresh every 60 seconds if server is online

Offline/degraded mode: when GET /api/mcp/tools returns ECONNREFUSED or 5xx, the provider: (1) shows a single tree item with label '⚠ Rorca server offline', description 'click to start', contextValue = 'rorcaOffline'; (2) retains the last-fetched tool list in memory so tree items are still visible but dimmed (TreeItem.description = '(cached)'); (3) 'Start Rorca Server' inline action on the offline item executes the 'rorca.startServer' command

Connection status indicator: VS Code status bar item shows '● Rorca' (green) when server is reachable, '○ Rorca' (amber) when offline — clicking opens the MCP Tools panel; status bar item disposed when extension deactivates
Server reachability is polled via GET /api/health every 30s; on status change (online→offline or offline→online), status bar updates immediately and tree view refreshes

Tool node context menu (right-click) includes: 'Copy Tool Name', 'Insert at Cursor', 'Copy as MCP Call' (copies JSON: { "tool": "rorca_tool_name", "params": { ... } } with required params as empty strings), 'View Documentation' (opens /api/docs#tag/<category> in external browser via vscode.env.openExternal)
Category nodes show child count as description: e.g. 'Specs & Pipeline' node shows description '11 tools' (9 existing + 2 new from MC-001/MC-002)
Tree view shows empty state message 'No MCP tools found. Is the Rorca server running?' when tool list is empty and server is reachable (handles case of server returning empty array unexpectedly)

The 'Rorca: Refresh MCP Tools' command (rorca.refreshMcpTools) appears in Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P) and triggers immediate re-fetch from /api/mcp/tools; shows 'Rorca: MCP tools refreshed (N tools)' information message on success
Tree items have accessible aria-label: tool name + category for screen reader support; category nodes have aria-label: '<category> category, N tools'

When rorca server returns 401 Unauthorized (auth enabled), tree shows single item: '⚠ Authentication required' with inline 'Login' action that opens /api/auth/login in external browser — does not crash or show cryptic error
The GET /api/mcp/tools backend endpoint is also annotated with @swagger JSDoc so it appears in the Swagger UI at /api/docs and is auto-included in any OpenAPI-to-MCP generation
Tool nodes display their required parameters count as a small badge or description suffix: 'rorca_generate_spec · 2 required params' — helps user understand complexity before inserting
Double-clicking a tool node (not just single-click) triggers the Insert at Cursor action — single-click selects/expands; this prevents accidental inserts when browsing

The extension's activate() function sets vscode.commands.executeCommand('setContext', 'rorca.extensionActive', true) on successful activation and 'rorca.serverOnline', false initially until first health check completes (within 5s of activation)

deactivate() function in extension cleans up all resources: disposes status bar item, clears health poll interval, disposes tree data provider event emitter, unregisters all commands — prevents memory leaks on extension reload

The tree view has a welcome content section shown when no tools loaded yet (first-time load): 'Connect to Rorca
Start the Rorca server then click Refresh.
[Start Server]
[Refresh]' — buttons trigger rorca.startServer and rorca.refreshMcpTools commands respectively
TreeItem iconPath for category nodes uses vscode.ThemeIcon('folder') (built-in); for tool nodes uses vscode.ThemeIcon('symbol-function') — no custom SVG files needed, reduces bundle size

userStories.title: CLI Shell Completion and Man Page
userStories.description: Add shell completion support to the rorca CLI so users get tab-completion for subcommands, flags, and workspace IDs in their terminal. Also generate a man page via the completions infrastructure. Uses the commander/oclif completion pattern: a hidden rorca completion command that outputs shell-specific completion scripts, plus a rorca man command that prints groff-formatted documentation.
acceptanceCriteria: rorca completion bash outputs a valid Bash completion script to stdout that, when eval'd or sourced, provides tab completion for: rorca <TAB> (shows: start, init, forge, run, status, approve, cancel, completion, man), rorca forge --<TAB> (shows: --workspace, --run, --json, --model, --spec-model, --auto-worktree, --api-url, --verbose, --help), rorca run --<TAB> (shows: --workspace, --json, --api-url, --verbose, --help), rorca status --<TAB> (shows: --watch, --json, --api-url, --help)

rorca completion zsh outputs a valid Zsh completion script using the #compdef format that provides the same completions as the Bash version; the script uses _arguments and _describe for structured completions
rorca completion fish outputs a valid Fish shell completion script using complete -c rorca format; supports --help descriptions on each subcommand and flag

Installation instructions printed after 'rorca completion bash': '# Add to ~/.bashrc:
eval "$(rorca completion bash)"
# Or write to file:
rorca completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/rorca'

rorca completion bash --workspace includes dynamic completion for --workspace flag: when user types rorca forge --workspace <TAB>, completion script calls rorca completion _workspaces (hidden subcommand) which fetches workspace paths from GET /api/workspaces (falling back to empty if server offline) and outputs one path per line for the shell to complete

rorca man outputs a man-page-compatible text document to stdout (groff/troff format) covering all subcommands with SYNOPSIS, DESCRIPTION, OPTIONS, EXAMPLES, and EXIT CODES sections; can be piped to man: rorca man | man -l -
rorca man --html outputs the same documentation as HTML to stdout for embedding in docs sites
The completion script handles the --api-url flag position-independently: completion works whether the user types rorca --api-url http://... forge <TAB> or rorca forge --api-url http://... <TAB>
rorca --version outputs semantic version from package.json (e.g. '1.0.0') and exits 0 — already exists but must be verified to still work after adding new commands
All new completion subcommands are hidden from rorca --help output (marked as hidden in commander) to avoid cluttering the main help, but are accessible and documented in rorca man
rorca completion bash is idempotent: running eval "$(rorca completion bash)" multiple times in the same shell session does not register duplicate completion handlers
rorca completion --help prints instructions for all three shells: Bash, Zsh, Fish — with the specific eval or source command for each

Completion script handles the case where rorca server is offline during --workspace completion: falls back to completing with filesystem paths using compgen -d (directory completion) rather than showing an error
rorca man --version outputs the rorca version at the top of the man page: '.TH RORCA 1 "March 2026" "rorca 1.0.0" "User Commands"'

userStories.title: VS Code Extension Settings Contribution Point Schema
userStories.description: Add a comprehensive settings contribution to the rorca VS Code extension's package.json so users can configure the extension via VS Code's built-in Settings UI (Cmd+, on Mac). Settings cover server connection, UI preferences, and default behaviors. Uses proper scope declarations to distinguish between user-global settings (e.g. server URL) and workspace-specific settings (e.g. default workspace path for the current project). Includes when-clause guards on commands so context menu items only appear when relevant.
acceptanceCriteria: package.json contributes configuration with title 'Rorca' and the following properties, each with type, description, default, and scope: rorca.apiUrl (string, 'http://localhost:3030', window scope, description: 'URL of the Rorca backend server'), rorca.defaultWorkspacePath (string, '', resource scope, description: 'Default workspace path for this project — overrides workspace autodetection'), rorca.autoRefreshInterval (number, 60, window scope, description: 'Seconds between automatic MCP tool list refreshes (0 to disable)', minimum: 0, maximum: 3600), rorca.showStatusBarItem (boolean, true, window scope, description: 'Show Rorca connection status in the VS Code status bar'), rorca.insertSyntax (string, enum ['name-only', 'json-call', 'slash-command'], 'name-only', window scope, description: 'What to insert when clicking Insert at Cursor in the MCP Tools tree: name-only (just the tool name), json-call (full JSON call object), slash-command (/mcp__rorca__tool_name)')

Extension reads rorca.apiUrl setting via vscode.workspace.getConfiguration('rorca').get<string>('apiUrl', 'http://localhost:3030') at activation and on any configuration change; registers vscode.workspace.onDidChangeConfiguration listener that re-fetches tool list when rorca.apiUrl changes

rorca.defaultWorkspacePath has resource scope (per-folder override) so a monorepo with multiple Rorca workspaces can set different defaults per VS Code folder; when set, rorca forge and rorca run commands in the terminal use this path as the --workspace default
When rorca.showStatusBarItem is false, status bar item is hidden (item.hide()) without disposing — so toggling back to true shows it immediately without reinitializing

package.json menus contribution adds context menu items to editor/context with when clause 'rorca.serverOnline' context key (set via vscode.commands.executeCommand('setContext', 'rorca.serverOnline', true|false) based on health polling): when true, shows 'Rorca: Forge from Selection' command in right-click menu for selected text

package.json menus contribution adds 'Rorca: Run Spec' to explorer/context with when clause 'resourceExtname == .json && resourceFilename =~ /^forge\/specs\/(approved|pending)\// && rorca.serverOnline' — only appears on spec JSON files in the right directories
All rorca.* commands registered in package.json include 'category': 'Rorca' so they appear grouped under 'Rorca: ...' in the Command Palette (Cmd+Shift+P)

Package.json contributes keybindings: Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on Mac) for 'rorca.forgeFromSelection' with when clause 'editorHasSelection && rorca.serverOnline' — inserts selected text as brief into rorca forge terminal command

Extension settings changes are validated: rorca.autoRefreshInterval rejects values > 3600 with a warning notification 'Rorca: autoRefreshInterval must be between 0 and 3600 seconds'; rorca.apiUrl validates URL format (must start with http:// or https://) and shows warning if invalid

A 'Rorca: Test Connection' command (rorca.testConnection) pings GET /api/health using the current rorca.apiUrl setting and shows: information message 'Rorca server is online (v1.x.x)' on success, or error message 'Cannot connect to Rorca at <url>. Check rorca.apiUrl in settings.' on failure

rorca.insertSyntax setting affects 'Insert at Cursor' behavior: 'name-only' inserts 'rorca_tool_name', 'json-call' inserts '{ "tool": "rorca_tool_name", "params": { "param1": "", ... } }' with all required params as empty string placeholders, 'slash-command' inserts '/mcp__rorca__tool_name arg1 arg2'
Settings are also editable via rorca.testConnection quick pick — after testing connection successfully, it offers 'Change Server URL' option that opens the settings UI focused on rorca.apiUrl
Package.json specifies engines: { 'vscode': '^1.74.0' } minimum version requirement (1.74 introduced tree view activation events as implicit from contributes.views)

Extension exports a public API: { getServerUrl(): string, isServerOnline(): boolean } via module.exports = { activate, deactivate } so other VS Code extensions can depend on rorca and query its status

userStories.title: MCP Tool Error Recovery and Offline Graceful Degradation
userStories.description: Implement error recovery and offline handling for the rorca MCP server so that tools fail gracefully with actionable error messages when the backend is unreachable, return structured errors that LLMs can act on, and implement connection retry with exponential backoff for transient failures. The stdio MCP server (mcp/server.ts) currently makes HTTP calls to localhost:3030 on every tool invocation — these need proper error wrapping and retry logic.
acceptanceCriteria: All existing 24 MCP tools in server.ts are wrapped with a shared error-handling function wrapToolCall<T>(toolName: string, fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<CallToolResult> that: catches ECONNREFUSED and returns { content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify({ ok: false, error: 'Rorca server is offline', tool: toolName, suggestion: 'Start the server: rorca start', offline: true }) }], isError: true }; catches timeout (>30s per tool call) and returns { content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify({ ok: false, error: 'Tool call timed out after 30s', tool: toolName, suggestion: 'The Rorca server may be overloaded. Try again.' }) }], isError: true }; catches non-2xx HTTP responses and returns { content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify({ ok: false, error: 'API error: <status> <statusText>', tool: toolName, body: responseBody }) }], isError: true }

Exponential backoff retry: ECONNREFUSED errors trigger 3 retry attempts with delays of 1s, 2s, 4s before giving up and returning offline error — only for tools that are idempotent (GET-equivalent tools: rorca_list_specs, rorca_list_runs, rorca_get_direction, rorca_list_workspaces, rorca_get_memories, rorca_workspace_stats, rorca_get_context, rorca_synthesize_direction, rorca_search_stories, rorca_run_status, rorca_pipeline_status, rorca_usage_stats); mutating tools (generate, approve, trigger, cancel, edit, delete, add, update, save, create, log, retry) do NOT retry to avoid double-execution

Cached tool list fallback: on server startup, mcp/server.ts attempts GET /api/mcp/tools and caches the tool list in memory; if subsequent calls fail, the cached list allows the MCP client to still see available tools even when the server is offline; cache is refreshed every 5 minutes when server is reachable

rorca_list_specs, rorca_list_runs, rorca_get_direction, rorca_list_workspaces, rorca_get_memories: when offline, return cached data if available with { ok: true, cached: true, cached_at: ISO-timestamp, data: [...], warning: 'Using cached data — Rorca server is offline' }

Connection health check: mcp/server.ts exports a startHealthCheck() function that pings GET /api/health every 30s; on status change broadcasts a server notification via server.notification({ method: 'notifications/rorca/connection', params: { online: boolean, url: string } }) so MCP clients can update their UI

rorca_forge_and_run specifically: if connection drops MID-RUN (after pipeline started but SSE disconnects), falls back to polling and emits a progress notification: { message: 'SSE disconnected, falling back to polling every 15s...', phase: 'polling_fallback' }

All tool result content uses JSON.stringify with 2-space indentation (not compact JSON) so LLMs can read the output without explicit JSON parsing: content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify(result, null, 2) }]

Request timeout: each HTTP call from mcp/server.ts to the backend uses AbortController with 30s timeout; timeout error message distinguishes from ECONNREFUSED: 'Tool call timed out after 30 seconds. The Rorca server is running but may be slow. Try again.'

Structured error objects always include: { ok: false, error: string (human-readable), tool: string (tool name), timestamp: ISO-string } plus optional: category, suggestion, offline, cached fields — this consistency allows LLMs to pattern-match on ok:false across all tools
MCP server logs errors to stderr (not stdout which is the MCP protocol stream): console.error('[rorca-mcp]', toolName, error.message) so debugging is possible without corrupting the JSON-RPC stream

AbortController timeout of 30s applies per individual HTTP call, not per-tool-total — rorca_forge_and_run can run for up to timeout_minutes; only each internal API call (generate, approve, trigger) is individually limited to 30s
The shared wrapToolCall function logs the retry attempt to stderr: '[rorca-mcp] rorca_list_specs retrying (attempt 2/3) after ECONNREFUSED...' — helps with MCP server debugging

Tool schema validation errors (Zod parse errors on input) return isError:true with { ok: false, error: 'Invalid input: <field> <zod error message>', tool: toolName } — these are NOT retried since the input itself is wrong
The health check subscription mechanism: if startHealthCheck() is called and later the process exits, clearInterval is called on the health check timer — no uncleaned timers leak on shutdown

userStories.title: CLI Non-TTY and CI Mode with Structured JSON Output
userStories.description: Ensure the rorca CLI works correctly in CI/CD environments (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins) where stdout is piped (non-TTY), environment has NO_COLOR or TERM=dumb, and scripts expect predictable exit codes and parseable output. Adds --json flag for machine-readable output, --quiet flag for minimal output, and explicit CI detection. Separates concerns: human feedback (progress, spinners, colors) goes to stderr in TTY mode; data (results, tables) always goes to stdout in a scripting-friendly format.
acceptanceCriteria: CI detection: CLI checks (in order) for CI=true env var, GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, GITLAB_CI=true, JENKINS_URL set, !process.stdout.isTTY — if any match, automatically enables non-TTY mode (no spinners, no ANSI codes, one-line-per-event output on stdout)

In CI mode, rorca forge --run outputs one line per event to stdout: 'story_started US-001 Add payment model', 'story_passed US-001 Add payment model 134s 0retries', 'story_failed US-003 Stripe webhook 245s 3retries', 'run_complete passed=7 failed=1 skipped=0 elapsed=489s' — all lowercase, space-separated, no ANSI codes, suitable for grep/awk

rorca forge --json outputs ONLY a single JSON object to stdout at run completion (nothing else on stdout during the run); all progress goes to stderr as plain text: 'Generating spec...', 'Pipeline started: run #42', 'US-001 passed (134s)', 'US-003 failed (245s, 3 retries)' — stderr output format is always plain text even when --json is active

The --json flag is supported by: rorca forge [--run], rorca run, rorca status — each outputs the same JSON schema: { ok: boolean, specId: string|null, specTitle: string|null, runId: number|null, passed: number, failed: number, skipped: number, elapsed: number, stories: Array<{id, title, status, elapsed, retries}>, error: string|null }

rorca forge --json without --run (spec generation only): { ok: true, specId: 'rorca-my-feature', specTitle: 'My Feature', storyCount: 8, runId: null, passed: 0, failed: 0, skipped: 0, elapsed: 12, stories: [...storyTitles as objects with status:null], error: null }

rorca --quiet flag: suppresses all stderr output (no progress lines, no elapsed time, no error context); only the final result summary (or --json output) is written to stdout; useful when piping rorca into other tools that would be confused by stderr interleaved with stdout

Exit code contract is documented in rorca --help and rorca man: 0 (success: all stories passed, or spec generated without --run), 1 (partial/user failure: one or more stories failed, spec generation error, spec not found), 2 (system error: ECONNREFUSED, unexpected 500, killed by signal), 130 (SIGINT: user interrupted), 143 (SIGTERM: process terminated externally)

SIGTERM handling: when rorca CLI process receives SIGTERM (e.g. CI job timeout kills the process), it prints to stderr 'SIGTERM received. Run is still active in Rorca (run #N). To cancel: rorca cancel <run-id>' then exits 143 — does NOT cancel the pipeline run (server-side run continues)

GitHub Actions integration: rorca forge --run outputs GitHub Actions workflow commands to stdout when GITHUB_ACTIONS=true: '::group::Rorca Pipeline Run #42' before first story, '::endgroup::' after last story, '::error::' prefix for failed stories, '::notice::' prefix for passed stories — these are rendered as collapsible sections in the Actions UI

rorca status --json <run-id> outputs: { runId: number, specId: string, specTitle: string, status: 'running'|'completed'|'failed'|'cancelled', elapsed: number, passed: number, failed: number, skipped: number, total: number, stories: Array<{id, title, status, elapsed, retries}> } and exits 0 regardless of run status (use .status field to check in scripts)

When any command encounters a non-zero exit scenario, the error message is written to stderr and the JSON (if --json) has ok:false with error field — this ensures stderr can be redirected to /dev/null without losing the error in --json mode

rorca cancel <run-id> command added as companion to forge/run/status: calls POST /api/pipeline/runs/:id/cancel, prints 'Run #N cancelled (7 stories completed, 3 remaining)' and exits 0; in --json mode outputs { ok: true, runId, status:'cancelled', storiesCompleted, storiesRemaining }

When CI=true and a story fails, rorca prints the story failure reason to stderr: 'story_failed US-003 Stripe webhook: Process exited with code 1 after 3 retries' — includes exit code and retry count from story_results row

The --verbose flag (all commands) prints to stderr: API URL being used, workspace ID resolved, spec model used, execution model used, worktree path if applicable — useful for CI debugging without polluting normal output

rorca run with --story <story-id> flag triggers single-story execution via POST /api/pipeline/trigger with storyId param, streams only that story's events, exits 0 if story passes or 1 if fails — useful for re-running a single failed story from CLI
